objective: Proof with exact finite computation. For each of the nine one-bit decorations (up to exchanging the labels) that exclude both crystals in ticket A, test the route by which a decorated law would force the pinwheel: composition at every level. (1) Every complete collar in the arc-consistent core of COLLAR-PLANE-20261108-001B's level-one law: can the labels of its central tile's five children avoid s(0) and s(1)? If never, parent labels are forced. (2) The labelled level-one law Q(s): labellings of core collars whose decorated cut gives every child a collar of the decoration's law. (3) Arc consistency on Q(s), with labels agreeing on shared tiles. (4) Whether every survivor is a labelled collar of the law itself; if so, composition is forced at every level and the decoration forces the pinwheel. Controls: the genuine labelled pinwheel collars survive, and a decoration that admits a crystal (ticket A) keeps a survivor outside its law.
status: Proved 2026-11-08 (ROUND-PRICE-20261108-001B-P001): a decoration forces the pinwheel if parent labels are forced and every surviving labelled level-one collar lies in its law; for the nine one-bit survivors of ticket A parent labels are forced but pairwise consistency leaves labelled level-one collars outside the law, so forcing is not settled; one of the nine (10001, 01100, with its relabelling) admits a period-4 brick crystal after three cuts, leaving sixteen one-bit candidates (eight up to relabelling).
title: Do the eighteen surviving one-bit decorations force composition?
